top.line: Ten hard conference questions, answered under journalistic challenge
top.para: My co-founder brought back ten questions buyers, investors and competitors ask, from bypass and liability to agent-to-agent delegation and metrics. I answered them in a two-hour interview with Claude acting as a detail-minded journalist, pushing until every answer was specific and the set held together.

s0.line: An ABP records mandate, reach, gap and barriers
s0.para: The Agent Behaviour Policy describes one agent in one deployment: the mandate (locked under change control), the grant or reach (measured against logs), the delta (derived, never authored) and barriers. Only a boundary counts as a control. Every engagement aims for the smallest mandate, reach, gap and self-policed residual.

s1.line: Ten challenges cover almost everything buyers will ask
s1.para: The questions: bypass of a $25k cap via a $75k order, future-proofing when a refund integration appears, tailoring and price, insurance and liability, differentiation, supply chain, who enforces, remediation, agent-to-agent instruction, and measurable outcomes such as coverage, false positives and return on investment.

s2.line: RiskMandate authors and pre-commits; the customer's stack enforces
s2.para: We sit outside the request path, so excess reach is surfaced before any action. The mandate is locked, so new capability lands only as excess. Liability stays with the customer and routes to executives. We make agents insurable, enable other vendors, treat the supply chain as a bigger agent, and measure reduction in accepted risk.

s3.line: We are not inline, not an insurer, not one-button
s3.para: Staying out of the request path keeps us a partner to every vendor and keeps liability off us. We carry no risk and place no cover. No single button can stop an agent, because that depends on each deployment, so we ask who can pull the plug instead.

s4.line: Much is design; the model and library are live
s4.para: The ABP model, library and example policies are live and free. The four priced levels exist but payment rails are incomplete and design partners are free. Reach recompute works for simple single-agent cases. Licence to Operate, the Insurability Index, reversibility and PKI delegation are design, plans or unwired MVPs.

s5.line: Our own site contradicts our position in three places
s5.para: Checked on 9 October 2026: the homepage claims "enforced in real time" with Blocked and Held cards, which should be framed as a customer integration pattern. The insurance page describes design as shipped. Level 1 is priced at £10 on two pages and £5 on the Licence to Operate page.

s6.line: Each answer, in full, rests on the reach-mandate gap
s6.para: A $75k order is possible only if reach allowed it on day one. Reach should be computed and wired to the pipeline; liability starts at the grant. We sell maintained open-source vaults, priced £10 to £1,500 then £5k to £100k engagements. Delegation needs PKI, and the headline metric is reduction in accepted risk.

s7.line: Others enforce; we make the gap visible and shrinking
s7.para: Across all ten answers, RiskMandate makes the gap between what agents should and can do visible, owned and shrinking, with each risk routed to a named executive. The answers are Dinis Cruz's, from a 9 October 2026 interview; the source of the 0.388 figure was not located.
